article.title: Iraq's cabinet completion raises Iranian influence concerns, but offers PM chance to curb militias
paras: The completion of Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi's Cabinet has renewed concerns about the continued influence of Iran-backed Shiite groups in Baghdad, particularly following the appointment of a senior militia leader and U.S.-designated terrorist as deputy prime minister. But some political observers say the appointments could offer al-Zaidi an opportunity to consolidate his authority and gradually bring armed factions under government control.

The debate reflects competing assessments of whether accommodating Iran-aligned political forces will further entrench their influence in Iraq's government or provide al-Zaidi with the political leverage needed to reduce their power.

Iraq's parliament on Thursday approved more than a dozen Cabinet appointments, completing the formation of al-Zaidi's government five months after it took office. Several key positions had remained vacant amid political disputes and concerns about Iranian influence.

Lawmakers approved Nayef al-Shammari as defense minister and Yasir al-Maliki as interior minister. They also appointed Laith al-Khazali, a senior leader of the Iran-backed Shiite militia Asaib Ahl al-Haq, as a deputy prime minister.

The United States designated Asaib Ahl al-Haq a foreign terrorist organization in 2020 and named al-Khazali and his brother, Qais, as specially designated global terrorists. Washington has accused the group of carrying out attacks against American and coalition forces.

The appointment has raised concerns, though, that Iran-backed armed groups continue to wield considerable influence over Iraq's political institutions, despite efforts to strengthen the authority of the central government.

Republican Rep. Joe Wilson condemned al-Khazali's appointment on social media platform X, describing him as a “designated terrorist and Iranian puppet” and calling for an end to Tehran's influence in Iraq.

“He is no better than ISIS, maybe even worse,” Wilson said of al-Khazali, using an acronym for the Islamic State terror group. “It is outrageous but sadly not shocking that he has been appointed deputy PM of Iraq.”
[[ https://x.com/RepJoeWilson/status/2110800674560823428?s=20 ]]

Despite those concerns, the United States has reaffirmed its support for Iraqi Prime Minister al-Zaidi, emphasizing the importance of Iraqi sovereignty and curbing the influence of Iran-backed armed groups.

“As President Trump made clear when he hosted Prime Minister Al-Zaidi’s historic July 14 visit, the United States strongly supports his vision to ensure a brighter future for all Iraqis,” a State Department spokesperson told VOA in a statement.
The spokesperson said Washington's goal remains a sovereign and secure Iraq capable of preventing attacks from its territory and maintaining strong relations with the U.S.

“Iran is an untrustworthy actor with a long history of using Iraqi militias to steal resources from the Iraqi people and threaten Iraq’s sovereignty,” the spokesperson said, emphasizing that U.S. efforts to promote regional stability focus on strengthening national sovereignty and economic prosperity.
Pragmatic approach to Iran-backed groups?

Former U.S. diplomat Joey Hood says the Trump administration may be willing to give al-Zaidi greater flexibility in dealing with Iran-backed militias, rather than opposing political arrangements that bring some of their leaders into government.

Hood told VOA that Trump and his special envoy to Iraq, Tom Barrack, appeared to favor an approach centered on economic partnerships rather than military operations or direct intervention in Baghdad's political decisions.
“They do not appear to be interested in micromanaging how the prime minister gains primacy over the Iranian-backed militias, unlike some previous U.S. administrations,” Hood told VOA.
He said Washington could adopt a wait-and-see approach, allowing al-Zaidi to use figures such as al-Khazali to bring less cooperative armed factions under control.
“If al-Zaidi succeeds in using al-Khazali and others to squeeze the uncooperative groups, he will have found an Iraqi solution to this problem,” the former U.S. diplomat said.

Hood said such an approach would place greater responsibility on al-Zaidi to demonstrate that political accommodation can translate into stronger government authority over armed groups, rather than allowing those groups to consolidate their influence from within the state.

The former ambassador to Tunisia cautioned that the ultimate test of al-Zaidi's strategy would be whether Iran-backed groups could continue exploiting Iraqis, influencing political decisions and launching attacks against Iraqi citizens and neighboring countries.
Political compromises raise spending concerns

Following the parliamentary vote to approve his cabinet, al-Zaidi pledged swift action to implement his government's priorities, promising continued efforts to deliver on commitments to the Iraqi people.

Beyond the question of Iranian influence, the cabinet expansion has also prompted criticism that the new Iraqi prime minister is creating government positions to accommodate competing political forces at the expense of Iraq's public finances.
Before Thursday's parliamentary session, a number of lawmakers protested and boycotted the proceedings, opposing the creation of several deputy prime ministerial positions and new ministries.
The lawmakers argued that the additional posts reflected the distribution of government positions according to political party quotas, at a time when Iraq should instead be reducing public spending.
Ghalib Aldaamy, a Baghdad-based academic and political researcher, told VOA that many Iraqis opposed the creation of new ministries and senior government positions.

Instead, he said, there had been expectations that the government would merge some ministries and abolish other institutions to streamline government bureaucracy and reduce pressure on the national budget.
zh: 伊拉克內閣組建完成引發對伊朗影響力的擔憂，但同時也為總理提供了遏制民兵組織的機會
伊拉克總理阿里·扎伊迪內閣的組建，再度引發外界對伊朗支持的什葉派團體在巴格達持續施加影響力的擔憂，特別是在一名高級民兵領袖暨美國列為恐怖分子的對象被任命為副總理之後。 但一些政治觀察家表示，這些任命或許能為扎伊迪提供一個機會，藉此鞏固其權威，並逐步將武裝派系納入政府控制之下。
這場辯論反映了各方對以下問題的相互對立的評估：接納與伊朗結盟的政治勢力，究竟會進一步鞏固這些勢力在伊拉克政府中的影響力，還是能為扎伊迪提供所需的政治籌碼，以削弱這些勢力的勢力。
伊拉克國會週四批准了十餘項內閣人事任命，在扎伊迪政府上任五個月後，終於完成了組閣工作。此前，由於政治爭端以及對伊朗影響力的擔憂，數個關鍵職位一直懸而未決。
國會議員批准奈耶夫·阿爾-沙馬里出任國防部長，並任命亞西爾·阿爾-馬利基為內政部長。他們還任命伊朗支持的什葉派民兵組織「正義派」（Asaib Ahl al-Haq）的高階領導人萊斯·阿爾-卡扎利為副總理。
美國於2020年將「阿薩伊布·阿赫爾·哈克」組織列為外國恐怖組織，並將阿爾-卡扎利及其兄弟卡伊斯列為「特別指定全球恐怖分子」。華府指控該組織對美軍及聯軍發動襲擊。
然而，這項任命引發了外界擔憂，認為儘管已採取措施加強中央政府的權威，但由伊朗支持的武裝團體仍持續對伊拉克的政治機構施加相當大的影響力。
共和黨眾議員喬·威爾遜在社交媒體平台 X 上譴責了阿爾-卡扎利的任命，稱其為「被列為恐怖分子的伊朗傀儡」，並呼籲終結德黑蘭在伊拉克的影響力。
「他跟『伊斯蘭國』（ISIS）沒什麼兩樣，甚至可能更糟，」威爾遜在談到阿爾-卡扎利時說道，並使用了這個伊斯蘭國恐怖組織的縮寫。「他被任命為伊拉克副總理，這雖然令人憤慨，但遺憾的是並不令人意外。」
[[ https://x.com/RepJoeWilson/status/2110800674560823428?s=20 ]]
儘管存在這些擔憂，美國仍重申對伊拉克總理扎伊迪的支持，並強調維護伊拉克主權以及遏制伊朗支持的武裝團體影響力的重要性。
「正如川普總統在7月14日接待阿爾-扎伊迪總理進行歷史性訪問時所明確表示的，美國強烈支持他為所有伊拉克人開創更光明未來的願景，」美國國務院發言人透過一份聲明向美國之音表示。
該發言人表示，華府的目標仍是建立一個主權獨立且安全的伊拉克，該國應能防止從其境內發動的攻擊，並與美國維持牢固的關係。
「伊朗是一個不可信的行為體，長期以來一直利用伊拉克民兵組織掠奪伊拉克人民的資源，並威脅伊拉克的主權，」該發言人表示，並強調美國為促進區域穩定所做的努力，重點在於強化國家主權與經濟繁榮。
對伊朗支持的團體採取務實做法？
前美國外交官喬伊·胡德表示，川普政府可能願意給予阿爾-扎伊迪更大的靈活性，以應對伊朗支持的民兵組織，而非反對將部分民兵組織領導人納入政府的政治安排。
胡德向美國之音表示，川普及其駐伊拉克特使湯姆·巴拉克似乎傾向採取以經濟夥伴關係為核心的策略，而非軍事行動或直接干預巴格達的政治決策。
「與某些前幾屆美國政府不同，他們似乎對細微管理總理如何在伊朗支持的民兵組織中取得主導地位一事不感興趣，」胡德對美國之音表示。
他表示，華盛頓可以採取觀望態度，讓阿爾-扎伊迪利用阿爾-卡扎利這類人物，將較不願合作的武裝派系納入控制之下。
「如果扎伊迪成功利用哈扎利等人向不合作的團體施壓，他便為這個問題找到了伊拉克式的解決方案，」這位前美國外交官表示。
胡德表示，這種做法將使阿爾-扎伊迪承擔更大的責任，必須證明政治妥協能夠轉化為政府對武裝團體更強大的管轄權，而非任由這些團體從國家內部鞏固其影響力。
這位前駐突尼西亞大使警告說，扎伊迪策略的最終考驗在於，由伊朗支持的團體能否繼續剝削伊拉克人、影響政治決策，並對伊拉克公民及鄰國發動攻擊。
政治上的妥協引發了對支出問題的擔憂
在議會表決通過其內閣人事案後，扎伊迪承諾將迅速採取行動，落實政府的優先要務，並保證將持續努力兌現對伊拉克人民的承諾。
除了伊朗影響力的問題之外，內閣擴編也引發批評，指稱伊拉克新任總理為了安撫相互競爭的政治勢力，正以犧牲伊拉克公共財政為代價來增設政府職位。
在週四的國會會議召開前，多名議員發起抗議並抵制會議，反對增設數個副總理職位及新部會。
議員們指出，在伊拉克本應削減公共開支之際，這些新增職位卻反映出政府職位是根據政黨配額進行分配的。
駐巴格達的學者暨政治研究員加利布·阿爾達米（Ghalib Aldaamy）向美國之音表示，許多伊拉克人反對增設新部會及高級政府職位。
相反地，他表示，外界原本預期政府會合併部分部會並廢除其他機構，以精簡政府官僚體系，並減輕國家預算的壓力。
